one_liner: Java NIO/epoll network framework whose stripped 'http-lite' TechEmpower entry ties lithium and cinatra (C++) on plaintext.
what_it_does: FireNio is an event-loop io framework for the JVM: a ChannelAcceptor/ChannelConnector bound to a NioEventLoopGroup, pluggable protocol codecs (HTTP/1.1, WebSocket, a length-value framing and a custom 'Protobase' codec) and an IoEventHandle callback that receives decoded Frames. It is its own API, not a Servlet or Netty replacement; you write handlers against Channel, Frame and ByteBuf. The TechEmpower entry is a hand-written platform-level server (hello/TestHttpLoadServer.java) built on firenio-all 1.3.6, not a web framework with routing.
how_it_is_fast: The lite HttpCodec (decode_lite) matches the method as a little-endian int, resolves '/plaintext' through a pre-built ByteTree of cached URLs, and skips GET headers entirely instead of materialising them as Strings; only Content-Length is read for POST. The TFB handler coalesces all pipelined responses of one read into a single pooled buffer and flushes it once from an event-loop task, using sun.misc.Unsafe-backed direct buffers, an optional JNI epoll binding instead of the JDK selector, per-event-loop frame caches and TCP_NODELAY. The only difference between the rank-5 'firenio-http-lite' and rank-34 'firenio' docker images is -Dlite=true and -Dcachedurl=true, so building header Strings in the full decoder alone costs about 20% of plaintext throughput (5,613,390 vs 7,004,779, derived from page data).
when_to_use: Studying how a JVM server reaches the 10 GbE plaintext ceiling: the TFB handler plus decode_lite is a compact, readable example of pipelined write coalescing and allocation-free request-line parsing.
Internal services on Linux where you control the client and only need GET/POST/HEAD with fixed-length bodies over HTTP/1.1.
Custom binary protocols on the JVM where a length-value codec and a small event-loop API are enough and you want to avoid Netty's size.
Benchmark baselines for a JVM entry in TechEmpower-style plaintext tests.
when_not_to_use: Anything that needs a maintained HTTP stack: last commit 2021-10-12, open crash and epoll-bind issues, no releases page, and the HTTP documentation lives on firenio.com rather than in the repository.

Realistic HTTP traffic: only GET, POST and HEAD are accepted (other methods throw ILLEGAL_METHOD, issue #65), there is no chunked Transfer-Encoding in either decoder, no HTTP/2 (issue #3) and no ALPN (issue #62).

Public-facing servers or anything behind a proxy that rewrites headers: lite mode ignores GET bodies and matches 'Content-Length:' case-sensitively, so a lowercase header leaves the body to be parsed as the next request.
Workloads that parse headers: the full decoder is 0.80x lithium in the same TFB round, so the C++ comparison only holds for the stripped lite path.

Modern JDKs without testing: the code targets Java 8 and reaches into sun.misc.Unsafe, the private DirectByteBuffer(long,int) constructor and sun.nio.ch.DirectBuffer; issue #58 reports illegal reflective access warnings and behaviour on JDK 17+ is not documented.

integration.form: Maven jar (com.firenio:firenio-all:1.3.6) with an optional bundled JNI epoll library
integration.dependencies: hppc 0.8.2; slf4j-api and wildfly-openssl-java as provided (optional) dependencies; the TFB entry adds jsoniter 0.9.23 for /json
integration.min_toolchain: Java 8 (pom source/target 1.8); the TFB build used OpenJDK 11 via maven:3.6.1-jdk-11-slim
integration.platforms: any JVM through Java NIO; the JNI epoll path is Linux only (Makefile builds a -m64 shared object with g++ -std=c++11 and no -O flag, shipped as a resource 'native.o' and loaded from a temp file) and needs direct-buffer support
integration.thread_safety: not documented; event-loop model with one NioEventLoop per (processors x core) thread, handlers run on the channel's event loop

gotchas: Epoll silently falls back to NIO when the native library or epoll_create fails (errors are logged only with a debug flag), so a deployment can run the slow path without noticing; the native code opens AF_INET6 sockets and fails with 'Address family not supported by protocol' on IPv4-only hosts (issue #57, open).

decode_lite assumes CRLF line endings and an ' HTTP/1.x' suffix (url_end = l_end - 10), parses Content-Length digits without validation, and never reads headers on GET; it is a benchmark parser, not a conforming one.

The TFB handler coalesces pipelined responses into one buffer allocated from the channel with buffer auto-expansion disabled and a pool sized at 32 MiB per event loop; the -Dframe and -Dlevel options in the dockerfile are only logged, not used.

Issue #66 (open) reports a JVM fatal error in Unsafe_SetNativeLong with firenio-all 1.3.6 on JDK 8 under Solaris SPARC; the maintainer asked whether epoll was enabled and the thread ends without a fix.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Against faf (Rust, rank 2) and wizzardo-http (Java, rank 8), which sit within 0.1% of it at the same TechEmpower plaintext ceiling, firenio offers nothing measurable; pick it only if you want the readable Java lite-codec example. For production JVM serving, Netty or Vert.x (both catalogued, maintained, full HTTP stacks) are the better choice.
verified_claims_summary: TechEmpower Round 22 plaintext (Dell R440, Xeon Gold 5120, 10 GbE, pipelined), read from a third-party screenshot: firenio-http-lite on OpenJDK 11 did 7,004,779 responses/s, rank 5 of 486, against cinatra (C++) 6,998,076 and lithium (C++, clang -O3 -march=native -flto with PGO) 6,993,976, a +0.10% to +0.15% tie at the network ceiling; the full-decoder 'firenio' entry did 5,613,390, 0.80x lithium (derived from page data).
status_note: Abandoned since October 2021 (7 open issues including a JVM crash and an epoll bind bug, no releases page) but Apache-2.0 and the lite codec plus TFB handler are small enough to read or copy as a pattern; not advisable as a production dependency.
